node.question: Using s1's inventory, can direct inspection produce a grounded map of paper boundaries, receiver overlap, and hidden contact regions, separately identifying what that map establishes or leaves unresolved about cup entry?
node.criteria: Pass when direct inspection supports a concrete boundary map and separately reported findings, even if the requested spatial relation remains unresolved. Report receiver identity as established cup, established non-cup, or unresolved; geometry as established entry, established wholly external placement, established rim-only placement, or unresolved; requested progress as established, excluded, or unresolved; and completion as established, excluded, or unresolved. Each finding requires visible reasons. Fail only when adequate visibility positively establishes absence of the relevant paper or any possible receiver; report this as object absence, not a boundary map. Unknown when visibility prevents even a grounded boundary assessment. A mapping pass earns no progress or completion credit. Wholly external placement requires affirmative evidence excluding entry elsewhere, not simply exposed corners, overlap, or lack of a visible opening. If entry geometry is established but cup identity is unresolved, requested progress remains unresolved.
node.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context and inspect the edited image independently. Identify each visible paper edge and corner by relative position. For every obscured segment, name the occluder, the visible endpoints if any, and its location relative to candidate receivers. Distinguish paper disappearing behind a receiver boundary from paper hidden only by the hand. Record local overlap ordering and its scope: foreground placement of one edge does not establish the placement of every paper segment. Test whether visible endpoints and boundary continuity exclude entry despite an obscured region, or whether a particular hidden contact region genuinely leaves entry undecidable. Do not assert generic hand occlusion without identifying the affected segment; equally, do not reconstruct hidden geometry without visible support. Inspect alternative receiving objects. Assess any curved line from its visible structure rather than assuming an opening or surface marking. Do not assume scene-specific colors, source correspondence, or cup identity. Return the boundary map before the four separately typed findings. Unsupported dimensions remain unresolved even when the mapping check passes.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible beside a blue, tapered cylindrical object with a broad circular opening and enclosing side walls, consistent with a cup. Edited: a blue printed paper/card with visible edges is held in front of a reddish rounded object. The reddish object’s visible curved outline and dark line do not establish a cup; its boundaries and any opening or enclosing walls are obscured by the paper and hand. The edited paper differs in appearance and shape from the source sheet, and the candidate receiving object cannot be reliably matched to the source cup from the visible features. Inventory is grounded, but edited cup identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved; insertion is not established.
